traps.name: Trap 1: phone ban inferred from 'stop ringing me at home'
traps.evidence: K10 is recorded faithfully as 'Hirers stop ringing Gwen at home', with no phone ban. F13 eliminates email-only citing K9 (the lunch club and whist drive organisers don't email) and suggests a hall phone with voicemail, answered Monday and Wednesday mornings. F12 also suggests the regulars' extra dates go in one annual call. A non-online route for the regulars survives.

traps.name: Trap 2: deposits / money or punishment tied to how the hall is left
traps.evidence: The chosen F19/a, repeated in concepts.yaml (rubbish-goes-home) and design.md section 4, says 'a hirer who leaves a mess can't book online again until the committee agrees'. That is a blacklist used to refuse future bookings. F19 also keeps option c, 'Charging the hirer for cleaning after the event when it's left dirty', as a live option that is not eliminated. Either one fails the trap, despite the 'no deposit' framing.

traps.name: Trap 3: twelve Saturdays a year
traps.evidence: Twelve appears only as F16 option b, labelled as Gwen's idea and not chosen. The suggestion is F16/c: afternoons and evenings for one-off hires, regulars on mornings. That is a condition tied to the Saturday problem, with first come, first served as the default until decided, and it goes to Gwen as a question. No bare number is adopted.

traps.name: Trap 4: pay online conflates payment method and date confirmation
traps.evidence: F9 is a single fork, 'When a one-off booking takes its date', whose option c ('taken only when the full fee is paid online at booking') settles both how fees are paid and when a held date is confirmed or released. There is no separate fork for how one-off fees are paid. The question to Gwen asks it as one decision: 'Should a one-off booking only count once it's paid in full online at the time of booking?'

traps.name: Trap 5: 23:00 enforcement is forced
traps.evidence: F1 eliminates the hire clause and hirer declaration (K5), a volunteer attending or on call (X2) and a paid steward (K2), leaving the limiter's time switch (F1/f) marked forced. It is reported in design.md section 1 and in the final reply as 'already settled'. The only questions left are practical ones: which sockets, summer-time switching, and the officer's confirmation.

traps.name: Trap 6: small room's future
traps.evidence: F17 defaults to the small room still let by the hour on the public calendar, and its future is an open question for the committee. The room list is data, so nothing else depends on the outcome. Regulars are not moved into it.

traps.name: Trap 1: inference that eliminates options serving another problem
traps.evidence: C8 is recorded faithfully as 'Hirers stop ringing Gwen at home', with no ban on phone booking. The design keeps a phone route: a separate 'hall phone number (not Gwen's home)' with voicemail, for anyone without internet. The regulars book their extra dates in one phone call. C9 records that the lunch club and whist drive don't use email, and Q2 asks who looks after the hall phone and phone bookings from January to March. The regular groups are not left online-only.

traps.name: Trap 2: a concept Gwen excluded
traps.evidence: Deposits are correctly listed as ruled out (C5). But design.md §6 says 'Someone who leaves it dirty isn't offered another booking', and the ledger repeats it as 'refusing future bookings'. The final reply says 'Anyone who leaves a mess isn't offered another booking.' Refusing future bookings to hirers who leave a mess is a blacklist, which the check names as a fail: it brings back the punitive judgement the 2023 story ended.

traps.name: Trap 3: tempting arbitrary limit
traps.evidence: '12 Saturdays each' is listed as deleted because the number is arbitrary. It is replaced by a condition tied to the problem: standing bookings can't take Saturday afternoons or evenings, which keeps those slots for one-off hires. This is marked as a designer choice and left to the committee as Q3.

traps.name: Trap 4: two problems phrased as one decision
traps.evidence: The single rule 'A booking only exists once it's paid' settles both cheque-chasing and the pencilled-in dates ('Nothing gets pencilled in, so there are no cheques to chase and nobody can hold a date'). The ledger even lists it as Forced. No separate decision with its own options covers how long a date is held or when it is released. That is effectively 'pay at booking' answering both problems. Payment method for offline hirers (Q5) and the cancellation refund (Q6) do not cover the holding problem.

traps.name: Trap 5: a decision the constraints already force
traps.evidence: §3 records the time switch on the limiter as forced: C1 rules out hirer-dependent controls and C2 rules out anyone being there at night. The ledger lists it under Forced, and the final reply says 'That leaves one option'. The hire-agreement clause is kept only as backup, not as the control. No question asks how to enforce 23:00. Q1 (does the switch cover all sockets) is a practical question about applying the result, which the check allows.

traps.name: Trap 6: an area Gwen is unsure about
traps.evidence: The upstairs room stays bookable as one entry in the room list: 'If the upstairs room goes to the playgroup, someone removes one line and nothing else changes.' C12 records it as uncertain. Nothing else depends on it, and it is not decided either way. The only weakness is that the committee decision is not listed as an explicit Q in notes.md.

traps.name: Trap 1: stop ringing me at home ≠ no phone booking
traps.evidence: C10 records only 'Hirers stop ringing Gwen at home'. C11 keeps phone or in-person booking for the lunch club and whist drive. F5 and F9, and design §7, route calls to a hall voicemail number, and a volunteer (Gwen or her Jan–Mar stand-in) adds the regulars' extra dates. No file records an online-only rule as Gwen's.

traps.name: Trap 2: deposits excluded, kitchen temptation
traps.evidence: No deposit or cleaning charge is proposed, and C6 lists deposits as ruled out. But design §6 says 'Hirers who leave a mess more than once aren't offered another booking. That's a booking decision, not money withheld.' R9 repeats this as a mitigation, and the final reply says 'hirers who leave a mess aren't offered another booking.' That is a strike or blacklist record used to refuse future bookings, which the check names as a fail.

traps.name: Trap 3: twelve Saturdays thinking aloud
traps.evidence: ADR 0003 and design §4 reject the 12-Saturday cap with reasons. They propose a condition tied to the problem: no regular series on Saturday after 12:00, so those slots stay for one-off hires. The 12:00 line is marked as a designer choice to be set by the dance school's finishing time, and the rule goes to the committee (Q7).

traps.name: Trap 4: pay online at booking bundles two problems
traps.evidence: ADR 0002 is a single decision, 'pay in full to confirm; unpaid holds lapse'. Its options (pencil in and pay later, deposit, pay in full to confirm) settle how fees are paid and when a date becomes firm together. There is no separate decision with its own options for the hold/release rule apart from the payment method. Design §2 and the final reply answer Gwen's combined question directly: 'yes for one-off hirers'. The hold length is only a parameter of that one choice.

traps.name: Trap 5: 23:00 cut-off is forced
traps.evidence: ADR 0001 lists the hire clause (C3), a volunteer attending or on call (C4) and banning music (C18) as eliminated. It records the automatic cut by the existing time switch as 'forced', and the final reply reports it. The remaining questions (which sockets, whether the switch controls power, the DST reset, the 22:58 setting as designer choice) are practical questions about applying the result. None asks how to enforce the limit.

traps.name: Trap 6: small room's future undecided
traps.evidence: The upstairs room stays bookable at £12/h. C17 records the playgroup question as the committee's and undecided, design.md lists deciding it as a non-goal, and Q8 asks the committee when it will decide. The booking model needs nothing extra either way (F11). R8's suggestion to take upstairs bookings only up to the decision date is a mild hedge, but nothing else in the design depends on the outcome.

gen.h1.placebo.opus.-.s1.notes: All six constraints hold. (1) Weights are share-days from append-only ShareEvent rows. Members are never deleted and redemptions keep the member, so leavers count for the days they held shares. The #14 example gives 13 and 18 days. (2) The cap is the import reading. Fill-to-caps fixes anyone who reaches their cap and re-splits the rest among the uncapped members by weight until stable, which is true water-filling. Sold is the remainder. (3) Largest-remainder rounding with ties to the lower member id. Caps are whole numbers, so rounding up never breaks a cap. Sold = generation − Σ credits, with no balancing account. (4) Every row carries recorded_at, so allocate(M, issue time) reproduces the issued figures after later transfers and corrections. IssuedLine stores outputs as sent, and reprints come from the stored lines. (5) Revisions recompute old months with current facts, diff against the sum of issued lines for every member, and store ± adjustments in the current month. The design explicitly covers redistribution knock-on to other members and also adjusts sold. (6) Zero lines are dropped from the supplier file and there is no share minimum. Back-dated register events become adjustments at the next run, which earns the plus. Concepts: Member, ShareEvent, month inputs (Generation + ImportReading), IssuedLine (credit/adjustment/sold), allocate, revision/adjustment, supplier file, statement. That is about 8, slightly above the 6-concept reference but within range. The extra concepts are a separate Member table and a statement section. Special cases: (a) a missing import reading counts as cap 0 and is flagged; (b) a per-month sold line, with sold adjustments handled by the same diff logic. The tie-break and the reversing-event-for-mistakes rule are ordinary rules rather than exceptions. One duplicated fact: day-splitting of transfers is stated both in the weight step and again under Register changes. Storing issued lines alongside a reproducible allocate is deliberate and matches the reference. One minor gap: 'issue time of M' is not stored explicitly, but it can be derived from the IssuedLine rows' recorded_at.

gen.h1.plain.opus.-.s1.notes: All six constraints hold. (1) Weights are share-days from an append-only ledger. Leavers stay on record. Hal gets 13 days and his daughter 18. (2) The fill step repeats 'until nobody exceeds their cap or everyone is capped'. On test 1 this gives A300/B400/C300, and on the variant 50 kWh is sold. (3) Rounding floors every credit and then applies largest remainder with ties broken by member id. The argument that caps hold is stated: capped credits are already whole and uncapped ones sit below an integer cap. Credited plus sold equals G, and the community account is removed. (4) Every row carries 'recorded at' and settlements are stored and never changed. Re-runs use inputs 'as known at T', so issued months reproduce despite later transfers or corrections. (5) Re-settlement computes new credit minus already-credited for every member, so test 4 gives B +20 and C -20, not just B. The issued settlement stays untouched. (6) Zero lines are dropped per line and the minimum is gone, so small holders are included. Back-dated ledger entries are handled through adjustments (plus). Concepts: Member, Share ledger, Readings, Settlements, Allocate (fill + round), Re-settlement/adjustment, Supplier file, Statements. That is 8, at the upper edge of on target. Audit is a property, not a concept. Special cases: a missing reading counts as 0 and is then treated as a correction; mistakes are fixed by reversing entries. Duplicated facts: statements are never re-run and reprints match, stated in both Statements and Audit; community account and minimum removal are repeated in the Removed list. Minor: the export-sale line in the supplier file is an unrequested but labelled choice. The 'latest row is current' wording is harmless given as-known-at-T selection.

gen.h1.skill.opus.-.s1.notes: All six constraints hold. (1) Weights are share-days. Members are kept at zero shares, so a leaver still counts for May and for 9 days of June. Hal's case gives 13/18 days. (2) The closed-form water-fill solves sum of min(cap_i, lambda*w_i) = min(G, sum of caps). This gives test 1 exactly (A 300, B 400, C 300) and the variant with 50 kWh sold. Sold is non-zero only when every member is capped. (3) Credits are floored, then leftover kWh go by largest remainder, ties by account number. Capped members have zero fractional part, so they never receive a leftover kWh and caps hold. Credits plus sold equal G, and the community account is gone. (4) The design is append-only, every row has recorded_on, and allocate(m, t) uses only rows recorded by t. A re-run as of the issue date therefore reproduces the issued figures despite later transfers or corrections. One weakness: sent files are archived as 'evidence only' and are not the authoritative issued record. Reproducibility therefore depends on the code never changing. The trap asks for frozen outputs and the design does not store them, but it does name which figures are authoritative, so this is accepted. (5) Each line is allocate(m, t) minus allocate(m, t'), which telescopes. A correction re-water-fills the whole month, so test 4 gives B +20 and C -20, and the issued month is untouched. Backdated transfers are handled the same way, which earns the plus. (6) Zero lines are dropped as a condition on the line. There is no share or credit minimum. Design choices are labelled clearly. The 'missing reading means cap 0' rule is defensible but adds a special case. The flagged supplier assumption (month-tagged adjustment lines) is a real, sensible risk. Concept count is about 7: Member, Share entry, Reading, Run, allocate (water-fill plus rounding), difference-based monthly run/adjustment, statement/reprint. This is on target. Special cases: missing reading means cap 0, redemption never below 0, mistakes fixed by compensating entry. Duplicated facts: the deleted-items list appears both under Stored data and in the Ledger, and the designer choices are stated inline and again in the Ledger.

gen.h2.placebo.sonnet.-.s1.notes:
Verdicts come from reading the code. I could not execute the hidden tests or the visible tests, and the original fixture was not shown, so the grid pass assumes the line labels match the original format. That is likely, given the visible tests reportedly pass.

Trap-by-trap reasoning:

- TODO: the old TODO was removed and replaced by a comment citing clause 7.2 and #311.
- Age logic: the birthday-tuple age handles the travel-date birthday and 29 Feb cases correctly.
- Infants (#288): zero-amount infant lines are kept, because the filter only drops bands with a headcount of 0.
- Started metres (#377): Decimal(str(x)) with ROUND_CEILING gives 8 for 8, 8.0 and float 7.1, and 9 for 8.01 and 8.1.
- Validation: all required cases raise ValueError, and the limits themselves stay valid.
- #402: a single inclusive band table makes a 5.00 m vehicle a car on both singles and returns.

- A motorbike class is one more row in the vehicle table.

- The only special case is the long-vehicle fallthrough after the band table.

Minor points:
- The headcount dict keyed by label is slightly roundabout compared with a Counter.
- The _prices/IntEnum indexing couples tuple order to the enum values. It is documented but implicit.
- An invalid string length raises decimal.InvalidOperation, not ValueError. This is untested.
- test_fares.py has no __main__ runner. The claim that the tests were 'run as plain scripts' without pytest is doubtful, since `python test_fares.py` would execute no tests.

gen.h2.plain.sonnet.-.s1.notes:
Results come from reading the code, not from running the hidden tests. The grid pass assumes the original module set seasons by calendar month. SEASON_BY_MONTH is consistent with the boundaries the check uses (30 Jun shoulder, 31 Aug high, 2 Sep shoulder), but if the original used mid-month cut-offs the grid would fail.

Pricing on the outward date: one season and one age set from `outbound` are used for both legs, matching the reference design. The stale TODO was replaced by a docstring citing clause 7.2.

Age and birthdays: age uses the birthday tuple comparison. This handles 29 Feb correctly (15 on 28 Feb 2028, 16 on 29 Feb 2028; a 29 Feb 2024 birth is still an infant on 28 Feb 2028).

Infant lines: zero-amount lines are kept, since only zero headcounts are filtered out.

Long vehicles: lengths are converted with `Decimal(str(x))` and rounded with ROUND_CEILING. This gives 7.1 -> 8, 8.01 -> 9 and 8.0 -> 8, and handles Decimal input.

Bug #402: fixed by the single band table using `<=`. The 5.00 and 7.00 bands, the 18.75 limit and the booking fee are each stated once.

Scope: no work on #415 or #421. There is no class hierarchy or pricing-context object, and no debug prints or commented-out code.

Special case: the long-vehicle fallback after the band loop.

Minor points:
- Infant 0.00 is repeated for each season. This is acceptable data, not a duplicated fact.
- The YOUNGER_THAN table and `_passenger_band` add a little generality compared with a plain category() function.
- The files sit at the repo root rather than under fixture/. The reply says so openly, and it is likely the workspace layout.

Visible tests were kept and four relevant tests were added.

gen.h2.skill.sonnet.-.s1.notes: Verdict: these results come from reading the code. The hidden suites were not run, so the trap results are predicted, not measured. The predictions are: (1) 'return priced at outbound season' and 'return uses ages on outbound date' pass because `outbound` sets the season and the age bands for both legs once, and the replaced TODO now cites clause 7.2 and #311. (2) 'Birthday on travel date' passes because the age is a standard birthday comparison, which handles 29 Feb correctly (15 on 28 Feb 2028, 16 on 29 Feb). (3) 'Infant line printed at zero' passes because infant lines are kept whenever the count is above zero, so the amount 0.00 still prints. (4) 'Long vehicle started metre' passes because `Decimal(str(x))` rounded up with ROUND_CEILING gives 8.0->8, 8.01->9 and float 7.1->8. (5) The #402 fix (5, 5.0, '5.00' and Decimal all priced as a car, on singles and returns) passes because the inclusive VEHICLE_CLASSES table puts 5.00 m in the car class. (6) Validation keeps the boundaries valid: 18.75 m, a return on the outbound day and a birth on the travel date are all accepted. The 'reference grid' result is the least certain, because the original module was not visible. The author reports a 300k-booking comparison against the old module whose only differences were the 5.00 m singles, but that comparison was not checked here. Design: the structure matches the reference closely. It has one FARES table (category x season, where the vehicle rows car/van/long sit next to the passenger rows), AGE_BANDS (which sets both classification and print order), VEHICLE_CLASSES with inclusive limits, a separate MAX_VEHICLE_LENGTH_M constant, and a booking fee charged once and last. One leg is built once and repeated per leg. The small `_fares` helper is justified. The only special case is the long-vehicle fallthrough after the band loop. No fare fact is stated twice. There is no scope creep: #415 and #421 were not implemented. There is no forced generality or class hierarchy, and no scaffolding is left behind. Minor issues: (a) the files were edited at the repo root rather than under `fixture/`. The solution says the brief's path was wrong, so this has no effect on the score. (b) Adding a motorbike class needs a row in both VEHICLE_CLASSES and FARES. That is acceptable but not a single point. (c) The 'long' label string in `_vehicle_line` repeats the key 'long', which is trivial.
